categories.main_business_segments: Peijia Medical operates primarily in three business segments: Transcatheter Valve Therapeutic Business, Future Technology Business, and Neurointerventional Business. The Transcatheter Valve Therapeutic segment focuses on products for aortic, mitral, and tricuspid valve diseases, including commercialized TAVR systems and pipeline products. The Future Technology Business, spun off from the Transcatheter Valve segment, develops cutting-edge heart valve therapeutic solutions such as lithotripsy valvuloplasty and robotic-assisted TAVR systems. The Neurointerventional Business develops and sells medical devices for cerebrovascular diseases, including hemorrhagic and ischemic stroke treatments and vascular access products.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages patented platform technologies including Non-glutaraldehyde Crosslinked Dry-tissue Technology, Polymeric Trileaflet Technology, and Lithotripsy Valvuloplasty Technology. Manufacturing is conducted in GMP-compliant facilities in Suzhou and Shanghai, with advanced quality management systems aligned with ISO 13485:2016 and Good Manufacturing Practices. Production includes cleanrooms and automated processes to ensure high precision and product quality. The company also employs innovative procedural techniques developed in collaboration with physicians to enhance clinical outcomes.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Peijia Medical primarily serves hospitals and clinical practitioners specializing in cardiovascular and neurovascular interventions. Its products target patients with valvular heart diseases and cerebrovascular diseases such as stroke. The company’s customer base includes over 2,000 hospitals in China, with approximately 650 medical institutions using its TAVR products and about 2,300 hospitals covered by its neurointerventional distributor network. The company also targets global markets through clinical trials and regulatory submissions, including the U.S. FDA.
categories.geographic_coverage: The Group’s operations and manufacturing facilities are mainly located in the People's Republic of China, with headquarters and production bases in Suzhou and Shanghai. It has established global R&D centers in Suzhou, Irvine (USA), and Boston (USA). The company’s products are distributed primarily in China, covering all 31 provinces and municipalities, and it is actively pursuing regulatory approvals and market expansion in the United States and other international markets.
categories.supply_chain_position: Peijia Medical operates primarily in the midstream and downstream segments of the medical device supply chain. It conducts in-house research and development, manufacturing, and commercialization of medical devices. The company manages its own production facilities and sales and marketing operations, positioning itself as an integrated medical device manufacturer and supplier directly serving hospitals and healthcare providers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic focus is on innovation in interventional procedural medical devices for structural heart and neurovascular diseases. It emphasizes advancing its TAVR product portfolio, including next-generation valves and robotic-assisted systems, and expanding its neurointerventional product lines. R&D priorities include clinical trials for pipeline products, platform technology development, and strategic spin-offs to enhance resource allocation. Collaborations with global partners and investment in intellectual property protection are key to its R&D strategy.
categories.revenue_model: Peijia Medical generates revenue primarily through the sales of medical devices, including commercialized transcatheter valve therapeutic products and neurointerventional products. Revenue is derived from product sales to hospitals and distributors. The company also benefits from licensing agreements, such as exclusive distribution rights for certain technologies in Greater China. Revenue growth is driven by increased sales volume, market penetration, and product launches.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Peijia Medical positions itself as a leading domestic innovator and competitor in the Chinese TAVR market, holding approximately 25% market share in the Chinese transfemoral TAVR segment and becoming an industry frontrunner in implantation volume. It competes with both domestic and international medical device companies, including global leaders like Edwards Lifesciences, which has acquired its licensing partner JenaValve. The company leverages its comprehensive product portfolio, innovative technologies, and strategic partnerships to strengthen its competitive position.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the year ended December 31, 2024, Peijia Medical reported revenue of RMB615.5 million, representing a 39.5% year-on-year increase. The company achieved a gross profit margin of 70.5% and narrowed its operating loss by 44.4% to RMB239.3 million. The Neurointerventional Business segment turned profitable with RMB52.1 million segment profit. Total assets stood at RMB2.69 billion with equity of RMB2.04 billion. The company has shown consistent revenue growth and operational improvements since its 2020 listing.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Peijia Medical emphasizes providing safe, effective, and affordable innovative medical devices that address unmet clinical needs in structural heart and neurovascular diseases. Its competitive differentiation lies in proprietary platform technologies, comprehensive product pipelines, and physician-centric innovation. The company offers a broad portfolio of transcatheter valve and neurointerventional products with enhanced durability, biocompatibility, and procedural efficiency. It also supports customers with extensive clinical education, innovative procedural techniques, and a strong distribution network.
